question: Through which part of the female reproductive system does the egg travel from the ovary to the uterus?
solution: The correct answer is __**Fallopian tube**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Fallopian tube** is a part of the female reproductive system that connects the ovaries to the uterus. • During ovulation, the ovary releases an egg (ovum) into the **Fallopian tube**, where it may be fertilized by sperm. • The movement of the egg through the Fallopian tube is facilitated by the coordinated actions of tiny hair-like structures called **cilia** and muscular contractions. • The Fallopian tube is the typical site of fertilization, where the sperm meets the egg to form a zygote. • Once fertilized, the zygote travels through the Fallopian tube to implant into the uterine lining, initiating pregnancy.
